skill.name: psp-construct
skill.description: Guides users through building a Pain Signal Profile for a specific ideal customer segment. Connects recent signals with operational pain, timing, roles, and recipient vocabulary.
skill.summary: Build a structured Pain Signal Profile using recent signals, specific operational pain, timing triggers, and recipient language.
skill.author: cmj-hub

content.value_statement: Broad customer segments and generic messaging make operational pain difficult to identify. This skill guides structured research linking recent signals, pain, timing, roles, and recipient vocabulary.
actual_capabilities: Guide users toward a specific ideal customer segment rather than a broad industry label.
Surface five to ten candidate signals across hiring, funding, product changes, leadership, content, and positioning.
Map the top three signals to specific operational pain and identify timing triggers.
Distinguish the role experiencing operational pain from the person authorizing a purchase.
Guide extraction of eight to twelve recipient phrases from five to ten sources, with optional WebFetch examples when available.
Produce a structured Markdown profile with five signals to monitor, then refine weak pain, timing, or vocabulary sections.
limitations: Configured as a sub-skill loaded by the parent psp skill, not as a directly invocable command.
Recent source retrieval depends on available tools and accessible pages; LinkedIn content may be unavailable.
Signal-to-pain mappings are research hypotheses, not proof of customer needs or purchase intent.
Does not implement continuous signal monitoring, outreach delivery, or automatic integrations with other workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Prospect Research
use_cases.description: Build a focused profile connecting recent company signals to the operational pain of a specific prospect role.

use_cases.title: Develop Segment Messaging
use_cases.description: Collect recipient language and connect it to operational pain before drafting segment-specific value propositions.

use_cases.title: Refine a Customer Segment
use_cases.description: Narrow a broad customer hypothesis and identify observable signals, relevant roles, and timing triggers for further validation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Guided Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PSP for [customer segment]. Help me narrow the segment, then guide me through signals, pain, timing, roles, and vocabulary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start a profile through the parent psp workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Candidate Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Construct a Pain Signal Profile for [specific segment]. Suggest five to ten candidate signals and map the top three to operational pain. Identify timing triggers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: develop a signal shortlist for a defined segment.

prompt_templates.title: Ground Vocabulary in Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PSP for [specific segment] using [five to ten public sources]. Extract eight to twelve recipient phrases. Separate supported observations from pain hypotheses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: use supplied sources to ground the profile in recipient language.

prompt_templates.title: Construct and Stress Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Construct a PSP for [segment] using [sources]. Distinguish the felt-pain role from the buyer. Identify timing triggers and five signals to monitor. Stress-test weak sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce a complete profile and challenge its weakest assumptions.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: build a PSP for Series-B SaaS companies with a product-led growth motion and a recent demand-generation leadership hire.
output: Segment: Series-B SaaS companies with a product-led growth motion and a recent demand-generation leadership hire.
Candidate signal: a demand-generation leadership appointment announced within 60 days; confirm the announcement date.
Pain hypothesis: the demand-generation lead needs to explain conversion gaps before the next pipeline review.
Timing: the new leader may be developing a 90-day plan.
Role: the demand-generation lead may experience the pain, while the CMO authorizes spending.
Vocabulary: pending recipient-written sources; no phrases have been verified.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: stress-test a profile that uses an old funding announcement and generic industry language.
output: Signal weakness: the funding announcement falls outside the suggested 30-day recency window.
Pain weakness: the profile describes a broad business goal rather than a specific operational moment.
Vocabulary weakness: the terms are industry language, not verified recipient phrases.
Revision priorities: find a recent signal, establish a timing trigger, and review five to ten recipient sources.

best_practices: Define the customer segment with concrete attributes before selecting signals.
Verify signal dates and source language before treating them as evidence.
Stress-test pain, timing, and vocabulary, and distinguish operational pain holders from purchasing authorities.
anti_patterns: Use a broad industry label as the complete customer segment.
Treat an inferred pain or timing trigger as a verified customer fact.
Invent recipient phrases or substitute generic category jargon for source language.

faq.question: What is a Pain Signal Profile?
faq.answer: It is a structured document connecting a customer segment with observable signals, operational pain, timing, a felt-pain role, and recipient vocabulary.

faq.question: How is this sub-skill activated?
faq.answer: The parent psp skill routes requests such as Build a PSP for a segment to this workflow. It is not directly invocable.

faq.question: Does it require web access?
faq.answer: WebFetch is optional for example research. Current signals and authentic vocabulary still require accessible sources or material supplied by the user.

faq.question: Which signals does it consider?
faq.answer: The workflow considers hiring, funding, product changes, leadership appointments, public content, and positioning changes. Suggested recency windows vary by signal type.

faq.question: Does a signal prove that a company needs my product?
faq.answer: No. A signal supports a pain hypothesis that needs validation. The workflow asks for specific operational pain and a relevant timing trigger.

faq.question: What does the final profile contain?
faq.answer: It includes segment precision, signal, pain, timing, role, vocabulary, and five signals to monitor. It also notes intended connections to messaging workflows.
